components.problem: Textbook kernel ridge regression is intractable on regular-grid climate fields under consumer hardware: an explicit N-by-N Gram matrix costs O(N^2) memory and the dense solve O(N^3), so practitioners default to randomized approximations (RFF, Nystrom, KISS-GP) without quantifying the accuracy loss, and climate-ML studies (deep ENSO forecasting, WeatherBench) are GPU/cluster-scale without CPU budget, memory, or flop/byte accounting. Corpus gaps G1-G4: no CPU-only exact KRR recipe for regular-grid climate fields (G1); resource accounting as first-class axis (G2); random-split leakage in field-reconstruction evaluation (G3); off-grid ENSO-index prediction from grid fields (G4).
components.method: Circulant-block KRR (FFT-KRR), with explicit structural honesty: a stationary kernel k(x-x') on a regular rectangular grid yields a block-Toeplitz-with-Toeplitz-blocks (BTTB) Gram matrix, not a circulant; exact spectral solution uses circulant EMBEDDING of the BTTB matrix (Dietrich-Newsam style) - the kernel is evaluated on an embedded (zero-padded) grid, diagonalized by the 2D FFT, solved as pointwise ridge-shrinkage (K_hat + lambda) * alpha_hat = y_hat, then the solution is read back from the embedded domain. Complexity O(N log N) training and prediction with O(N) memory; the embedding boundary/aliasing error is QUANTIFIED EMPIRICALLY (padding size sweep, error vs exact dense solve on subsampled grids) and reported - no unverified exactness claims. For masked/partial training inputs (T1b) exact single-shot spectral solve does not apply; we use an FFT-preconditioned conjugate gradient solve on the observed-subset system, reporting iteration counts, wall-clock, and memory, with no claim of one-shot exactness in the masked regime. Off-grid prediction (ENSO index from field) uses trigonometric interpolation of stationary kernel cross-covariances in O(N log N). Implementation: NumPy/SciPy FFT only; kernels: Matern(3/2), Matern(5/2), squared-exponential (all stationary), plus periodic-time x spatial product for ENSO.
components.experiment_design: Substrate: NOAA-family SST anomaly fields - Kaplan SST v2 (5-degree grid, 72x36 = 2592 cells/field, monthly, 1950-2023) from NOAA PSL if fetchable; else bundled synthetic-from-physics fields with explicit simulation markers in all artifacts/paper. Task T1 (reconstruction): masked-field imputation with masks as PREDICTION TARGETS ONLY, training on complete fields (no masked-train confusion); regimes: (a) exact spectral imputation of 10/30/50% random-pixel masks and spatial-block masks, evaluated under leave-one-field-out CV (48 held-out months) and spatial-block CV; (b) FFT-preconditioned CG with masked training inputs (10/30/50%), reporting iteration/wall-clock/memory. Task T2 (regression): Nino3.4 monthly index from full fields and from reconstructed fields under 5-fold time-block CV. Baselines (scikit-learn), commensurable via cost-swept sizes: exact KernelRidge on subsamples n in {2k, 5k, 10k}, Nystrom landmarks in {500, 2k, 5k, 10k}, RFF features in {500, 2k, 5k, 10k}. Metrics: RMSE, R2, predictive-interval coverage via SPLIT-CONFORMAL on held-out fields (defines calibration axis), wall-clock, peak RSS (resource.MemoryUsage), estimated flops and bytes per fit. Budget arithmetic (all arms sum well under 90 min / 7 GB / 12 cores): spectral fits at N=2592 are microsecond-scale FFTs; CG regime ~ 1000 iterations x 3 FFTs x 2592 x log(2592) flops; exact-KRR n=10k solve ~ 1e12 flops (BLAS, ~minutes); all baselines swept over 4 sizes. Ablations: padding-size embedding error, kernel choice, ridge lambda sweep (log grid, 8 values), random-split vs block-CV optimism gap (G3 measurement).

revisions_applied: BTTB-vs-circulant honesty: method now states BTTB structure and uses circulant embedding with empirically quantified boundary error (no unqualified exact-circulant claim)
Masked-input reconciliation: (T1a) masks as prediction targets only with training on complete fields; (T1b) FFT-preconditioned CG for masked training with explicit iteration/resource reporting
Budget arithmetic added: N per field, number of fields/folds, kernel/lambda grid sizes, per-arm flop/wall-clock estimates; total well under 90 min
Predictive intervals pinned: split-conformal on held-out fields with coverage + width metrics
Baselines made commensurable: Nystrom/RFF sizes swept {500,2k,5k,10k} and subsample n {2k,5k,10k}, accuracy-vs-cost frontier as the comparison axis
